newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: ANZ Bank sees good value in NZ IIB tender.
newsitem.headline: ANZ Bank sees good value in NZ IIB tender.

text.p: ANZ Investment Bank said on Tuesday the government's inflation-indexed bond tender on Thursday would offer investors a good opportunity to lock in high real yields.
The bank is forecasting a yield of 5.1 to 5.3 percent for the NZ$50 million worth of the IIB bonds, which mature in February 2016 and have a coupon of 4.5 percent.
Thursday's tender is the first index-linked tender of the 1997/98 fiscal year.
The government intends to issue $300 million IIBs in six tenders over the next 12 months as part of the $1.8 billion government bond programme announced in the June 26 budget.
"This will serve to further gradually increase IIB liquidity," ANZ said.

"$573 million of these bonds have been tendered since their reintroduction at the beginning of the 1995/96 fiscal year, so that approximately $590 million, including the indexation component, are now outstanding in the market."
ANZ said a notable feature of the market for these securities had been the surge in offshore interest in recent months.
It said non-resident holdings had risen to almost 63 percent at the time of the last Reserve Bank of New Zealand survey in July, up from around 22 percent at the same time last year.

"The introduction of similar bonds in the U.S. (TIPS) has sparked interest amongst many international investors towards these securities generally, and has seen the emergence of new international 'real return' funds," ANZ said.
The results of the bond tender will be announced by the RBNZ at 1.00 p.m. (0100 GMT) on Thursday.
